issues.legal_issue: A claimant who was present when the compensation award was made must seek a reference within the time running from the award, without requiring separate notice of the award.
material_facts: Acquittance records showed that claimants received compensation without protest on the day the award was made; two claimants who were not present that day received compensation two days later.
The reference was made long after the award, following writ proceedings, and the claimants argued that limitation had not begun because notice of the award had not been served.
issues.conclusion: For claimants present when the award was made, separate notice under Section 12(2) was unnecessary and the application had to be made within six weeks of the award; the reference was barred by limitation.
issues.legal_principle: Under the proviso to Section 18(2) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, a person present or represented before the Collector when the award is made must apply within six weeks of the award. Notice under Section 12(2) is relevant to the limitation rule for other cases, not for a claimant present at the award. The Court relied on no earlier case in stating this principle.

predicates.appeal_from_reference_award: The proceeding is an appeal challenging an award made on a reference for compensation for acquired land.
predicates.claimant_present_when_award_made: The claimant was present or represented before the acquiring officer when the compensation award was made.
predicates.application_after_applicable_deadline: The claimant sought the reference after the time allowed for a claimant in those circumstances had expired.

issues.definition: When a claimant present at the award seeks a reference after the applicable deadline, the reference is time-barred.

issues.legal_issue: A person who accepts compensation without protest is not entitled to seek a reference for determination of higher compensation.
material_facts: The claimants accepted the compensation awarded for their land without protest.
They later sought a reference to obtain increased compensation.
issues.conclusion: Claimants who received compensation without protest were not entitled to seek a reference under Section 18.
issues.legal_principle: The second proviso to Section 31(2) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, precludes a person who receives compensation without protest from seeking a reference under Section 18. The Court relied on no earlier case in stating this principle.

predicates.land_acquisition_reference_proceeding: The proceeding seeks a reference to determine compensation for acquired land.
predicates.compensation_accepted_without_protest: The claimant accepted the compensation offered without expressing protest.

issues.definition: In a proceeding for a reference on compensation, accepting compensation without protest means the claimant cannot seek the reference.

issues.legal_issue: A person joined to a compensation reference as a third party cannot claim higher compensation without independently satisfying the requirements for seeking a reference.
material_facts: Additional persons were impleaded in the reference after it had been made.

The judgment identified the original qualifying claimants as those who received compensation under protest and applied for a reference, and held that the impleaded persons had no right to claim higher compensation through that reference.
issues.conclusion: The impleaded third parties had no right to claim higher compensation by joining the reference; only claimants who received compensation under protest and applied for a reference could seek one.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 18(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, only a claimant who receives compensation under protest and makes an application for a reference is entitled to seek it. Impleading third parties does not allow them to circumvent that process. The Court relied on no earlier case in stating this principle.

predicates.land_acquisition_reference_proceeding: The proceeding is a reference seeking determination of compensation for acquired land.
predicates.third_party_joined_after_reference: A person who was not an original reference applicant was added to the proceeding after the reference had been made.
predicates.third_party_lacked_qualifying_applicatio: The added person had not independently made the required application after receiving compensation under protest.

issues.definition: A person added to a land-compensation reference who did not independently make a qualifying application cannot use that proceeding to claim higher compensation.
